(NYSE: PFE ) today announced detailed results across serotypes from a Phase 2 study ( NCT06524414 ) for its investigational 25-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidate, PF-07872412 (25vPnC), in infants. In the study, a four-dose series of 25vPnC elicited robust immune responses against all 25 serotypes and showed safety and tolerability comparable to four doses of PREVNAR 20 ® (Pneumococcal 20-valent Conjugate Vaccine). These findings were shared today in an oral presentation at IDWeek 2026 in Washington, D.C. 1 These data support the ongoing Phase 3 development program for 25vPnC, which, if successful, could help provide protection against serotypes collectively responsible for approximately 84% of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) cases among children under five years of age in the U.S . 2 “These encouraging data build on more than 25 years of progress in protecting children from serious pneumococcal disease with PREVNAR vaccines. By expanding serotype coverage and applying next-generation technology to the historically challenging serotype 3, this candidate aims to extend the substantial reductions in disease that existing vaccines have achieved. If successful, it could help provide children with the broadest protection against invasive pneumococcal disease to date.” — Annaliesa Anderson, Ph.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Vaccines Officer, Pfizer Phase 2 Study Results Across 25 Serotypes The Phase 2 study is evaluating the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of the 25-valent vaccine candidate (25vPnC) compared with PREVNAR 20 in healthy infants. These data build on results announced earlier this year showing: Robust immune responses against all 25 serotypes one month after Dose 3 and one month after Dose 4, including against all five new serotypes (15A, 23A, 23B, 24F, and 35B). Rates of local reactions, systemic events, and adverse events were balanced across the 25-valent vaccine candidate and PREVNAR 20 groups in the Phase 2 trial. Adverse events were consistent with conditions commonly diagnosed in this age group. There were no related serious adverse events identified in the study. 1 The 25-valent vaccine candidate elicited an enhanced immune response against serotype 3 compared with PREVNAR 20, generating GMCs that were 8.8-fold higher one month after Dose 3 and approximately 15-fold higher one month after Dose 4. 1 It utilizes next-generation technology specifically designed to elicit a more robust immune response against serotype 3, which accounts for 10.6% of all IPD in children under five years old in the U.S . 2 25-valent vaccine candidate also elicited functional responses in the opsonophagocytic activity assay (OPA) one month after Dose 4 for all 25 target serotypes, demonstrating booster effects. 1 This result demonstrates the vaccine candidate’s potential to generate antibodies that can contribute to the functional killing of pneumococcal bacteria.

The 1,500 mg every four weeks regimen (n=217) showed a least-squares mean reduction of 5.6 points from baseline in ESSDAI score, compared with 3.8 points for placebo (difference of 1.8 points; adjusted p<0.001). CAPLYTA significantly improved manic symptoms and overall illness severity versus placebo at Week 3, with significant improvements observed as early as Day 3. 1 The results were featured as a late-breaking presentation at the 2026 Neuroscience Education Institute (NEI) Fall Congress (November 5-8, Colorado Springs, CO). At 52 weeks, Foundayo met the primary endpoint, significantly reducing the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), the standard measure of sleep apnea severity, as well as improving weight and other cardiovascular risk factors. 1 The results were presented today at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 and simultaneously published in JAMA . OSA affects an estimated 936 million adults worldwide, and most have never been diagnosed. 2 In people with OSA, the airway repeatedly collapses during sleep, causing drops in oxygen and increases in blood pressure that are associated with hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease and stroke. 3,4 The AHA counts healthy sleep among its Life's Essential 8 measures of cardiovascular health and recommends screening for OSA in people with certain cardiovascular conditions, reflecting growing recognition that treating OSA is part of comprehensive cardiovascular care. 3,5 Vaishnavi Kundel , M.D., M.S., Associate Professor of Medicine, Division of Pulmonary , Critical Care and Sleep Medicine, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai : "We know there's a two-way relationship between sleep and cardiovascular health, and the repeated drops in oxygen that happen with obstructive sleep apnea can strain blood pressure and the heart over time. In ATTAIN-OSA, Foundayo significantly reduced breathing interruptions and drops in oxygen during sleep, while also improving blood pressure and inflammation. In addition to improving their sleep, what I care about for my patients is improving the cardiovascular risk factors that have the potential to impact long-term health." (November 7, 2026) – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced new patient experience findings a from the Phase 2 DAHLIAS study of nipocalimab in Sjögren’s disease (SjD), a chronic, systemic autoantibody-driven disease affecting approximately four million people worldwide. 1 The results show that mouth dryness is the symptom improvement that matters most to patients, 2 complementing previously reported Phase 2 study results on increased saliva production in patients who received nipocalimab. 3 This was also the most frequently reported symptom, with 96% of patients surveyed citing mouth dryness. 2 These findings helped to inform the design of the ongoing Phase 3 study of nipocalimab in SjD, and are among 23 abstracts on nipocalimab to be presented at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026. Patient experience of Sjögren’s disease reflects core symptoms including dryness and systemic manifestations Interviews were conducted with participants following the Phase 2 study’s treatment period. Five core symptoms were most frequently reported by patients: mouth dryness (96%), fatigue (92%), eye dryness (90%), joint pain (73%) and, among women, vaginal dryness (49%). Patients who participated in the interviews reported improvements across many of these core symptoms during the treatment phase of the study. 2 “Patients told us that Sjögren’s disease affects nearly every aspect of daily life, with mouth dryness emerging as both the most frequently reported symptom and the symptom most often prioritized, among those asked, for improvement,” said Ghaith Noaiseh, M.D., Associate Professor, Allergy, Clinical Immunology, and Rheumatology, The University of Kansas Medical Center. d “Notably, in the previously published clinical data, at least 50% improvement in objective salivary flow was observed in more than twice as many patients receiving 15 mg/kg nipocalimab compared with placebo. c I look forward to the Phase 3 results and what they may tell us about the potential of nipocalimab to deliver meaningful benefit for patients.” Symptom improvements were associated with tangible improvements in everyday life and functioning Patients described the core symptoms of SjD as having far-reaching effects on physical, social and emotional well-being, with improvements in these symptoms reported to have tangible benefits in day-to-day life. These improvements are associated with positive changes in physical functioning, less need for disease management, and less interference in family, work and social commitments. Nearly three-quarters of participants (73.5%) reported being satisfied or very satisfied with study treatment. 2 “These patient insights reinforce the broad, systemic nature of Sjögren’s disease and the importance of recognizing and addressing the symptoms and outcomes that matter most to patients,” said Leonard L. lead: Positive Phase 3 IDEAL Study Results Further Support Livdelzi®’s (Seladelpar) Impact on Achieving ALP Normalization Goals in Second-Line Treatment Across a Broad Population of People Living with Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) Back - Data to be Presented at The Liver Meeting ® Demonstrate Rapid and Sustained Improvements in ALP Levels with Livdelzi in Adults with PBC and ALP Levels Between 1-1.67 × ULN, Despite Receiving UDCA or with Intolerance to UDCA - - Gilead Will Engage Global Regulatory Authorities Based on These Results - FOSTER CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced the detailed results from the Phase 3 IDEAL study, which demonstrated that the majority of participants living with PBC and treated with Livdelzi ® (seladelpar) achieved the alkaline phosphatase (ALP) normalization composite endpoint defined as a composite of ALP ≤ 1.0× upper limit of normal (ULN) and a ≥ 15% decrease from baseline. ALP is a key marker of disease activity and long-term outcomes in PBC. These results can expand understanding of treatment effects and inform evolving treatment goals for people living with PBC. Key Highlights At Week 52, 75.4% (49/65) of participants who received Livdelzi achieved the ALP normalization composite endpoint versus 16.1% (5/31) of participants receiving placebo. Results will be presented at The Liver Meeting ® 2026, hosted by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD), November 5-9 in Denver, Colorado, and have been accepted for upcoming publication in the Journal of Hepatology. Gilead is engaging with global regulatory authorities to discuss these results. IDEAL is a Phase 3, randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled clinical study evaluating Livdelzi in adults living with PBC who have ALP levels above normal yet below the 1.67× ULN threshold typically required for inclusion in other PBC randomized controlled trials (RCTs). It is the first clinical trial to evaluate Livdelzi in people with inadequately controlled disease defined as ALP levels of 1-1.67× ULN despite receiving ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) for 12 months or with intolerance to UDCA. “People with PBC whose alkaline phosphatase remains elevated but below 1.67 times the upper limit of normal have been largely excluded from previous pivotal trials of second-line therapies,” said Cynthia Levy, MD, University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. “IDEAL provides randomized, placebo-controlled evidence that seladelpar can improve biochemical response in this population. These findings can inform individualized treatment discussions, taking into account each individual’s risk of disease progression, symptoms, and potential benefits and risks of additional therapy.” ALP is a key marker of disease activity with levels above normal associated with an increased risk of disease progression and poorer long-term outcomes, such as liver failure. Historically, the threshold for clinical study inclusion has been ALP levels >1.67× ULN. Recent clinical guidance recognizes ALP normalization as an ideal treatment goal in PBC. Results from IDEAL expand the evidence base by demonstrating that a significantly higher proportion of people with baseline ALP levels between 1-1.67× ULN and treated with Livdelzi can achieve ALP normalization compared to placebo. The response was evident after one month of treatment (52.3% versus 6.5% receiving placebo) and sustained through Week 52. “The IDEAL study evaluated the impact of initiating second-line treatment in people living with PBC who have lower levels of baseline ALP elevation compared to prior clinical trials,” said Swati Tole, MD, MS, Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, Inflammation, Gilead Sciences. “A significantly greater proportion of people with elevated ALP levels, but below the threshold typically studied, achieved ALP normalization with Livdelzi, supporting ALP normalization as an achievable treatment goal. Intellia Therapeutics Completes Enrollment in Phase 3 MAGNITUDE-2 Trial of Nexiguran Ziclumeran (Nex-z) for Patients with Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis with Polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN) November 4, 2026 PDF Version CAMBRIDGE, Mass. , Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Intellia Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTLA), a leading biopharmaceutical company focused on revolutionizing medicine leveraging CRISPR gene editing and other core technologies, today announced the completion of enrollment in MAGNITUDE-2, the Phase 3 clinical trial of nex-z in patients with ATTRv-PN. Nex-z is an investigational in vivo CRISPR-based therapeutic candidate designed to inactivate the TTR gene in the liver, thereby preventing the production of transthyretin (TTR) protein. Nex-z offers the possibility of halting and reversing disease by driving a rapid, deep, consistent and potentially lifelong reduction in TTR protein after a one-time treatment. “We are grateful to the patients, caregivers and investigators who are participating in MAGNITUDE-2,” said John Leonard , M.D., Intellia President and Chief Executive Officer. “Completing enrollment in this trial is a pivotal step toward bringing a potentially transformative one-time treatment to people living with ATTRv-PN, a debilitating and life-threatening disease with significant unmet need.” “While disease-modifying therapies have advanced the standard of care for ATTRv-PN, many patients continue to progress,” said John L. Berk , M.D., Professor Emeritus of Medicine, Amyloidosis Center, Boston University School of Medicine . “An agent that can quickly, substantially and consistently reduce TTR after a single dose would be a meaningful advancement for patients. Completing enrollment in the MAGNITUDE-2 trial is an exciting milestone toward that goal.” MAGNITUDE-2 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of nex-z in approximately 60 patients with ATTRv-PN. Adult patients with ATTRv-PN were randomized 1:1 to receive a single 55 mg infusion of nex-z or placebo. The primary endpoints of the trial are the change in modified neuropathy impairment score at month 18 and the change in serum TTR levels at day 29. Patients are eligible for optional blinded crossover following month 18. For more information on MAGNITUDE-2 (NCT06672237), please visit clinicaltrials.gov . Nex-z is also being investigated in MAGNITUDE, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of nex-z in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). For more information on MAGNITUDE (NCT06128629), please visit clinicaltrials.gov .

Merck Initiates Phase 3 Study Evaluating OHTUVAYRE® (ensifentrine) for the Prevention of COPD Exacerbations in Adult Patients Receiving Standard of Care With a History of Exacerbations Save November 3, 2026 6:45 am EST ENHANCE-3 study represents Merck’s commitment to addressing the burden of COPD exacerbations OHTUVAYRE ® is the first and only novel inhaled mechanism for the maintenance treatment of COPD in more than 20 years to combine bronchodilation and non-corticosteroid anti-inflammatory effects RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, today announced the initiation of ENHANCE-3 ( NCT07874815 ), a Phase 3 randomized clinical trial evaluating OHTUVAYRE (ensifentrine) for the prevention of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations in adult patients receiving standard of care (SOC) with a history of exacerbations. Recruitment of the ENHANCE-3 trial has begun, and the first patients are now enrolling in the United States. “Many patients with COPD continue to experience persistent symptoms such as shortness of breath, despite current standard-of-care therapy. For these patients, exacerbations remain a major driver of disease progression and diminished quality of life,” said Dr. Mahesh Patel, vice president, global clinical development, Merck Research Laboratories. “The initiation of the Phase 3 ENHANCE-3 study marks an important step in our efforts to further strengthen the body of evidence supporting OHTUVAYRE and its potential to address significant unmet needs in COPD care. We remain committed to advancing innovative research to help the millions of people impacted by this disease worldwide.” The ENHANCE-3 Phase 3 trial plans to enroll approximately 2,136 patients in 28 countries across the world. The primary endpoint of the study is the annualized rate of adjudicated moderate or severe COPD exacerbations, and secondary endpoints include lung function, health-related quality of life, severe exacerbations and safety. We look forward to sharing the results of the ENHANCE-3 trial with regulatory authorities globally. Based on the ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2 studies, OHTUVAYRE was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in June 2024 for the maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in adult patients. OHTUVAYRE is the first and only novel inhaled mechanism for the maintenance treatment of COPD in more than 20 years to combine bronchodilation and non-corticosteroid anti-inflammatory effects. OHTUVAYRE is also being evaluated in a Phase 2 clinical trial for the treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis.

lead: Neurocrine Biosciences Initiates Phase 2 Clinical Study Evaluating NBI-'567 in Adults with Alzheimer's Disease 10/20/26 Download PDF version SAN DIEGO , Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced the initiation of its Phase 2 clinical study of investigational compound NBI-1117567 (NBI-'567) in adults with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. NBI-'567 is an orally administered, M1/M4 (M1 preferring) selective muscarinic agonist being evaluated as an adjunctive treatment for cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's disease. NBI-'567 is designed to directly activate M1 and M4 muscarinic receptors, which are involved in neuronal circuits associated with learning and memory. The study will evaluate the potential of NBI-'567 to improve cognitive performance in adults with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease who are receiving stable treatment with an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor. "As a defining characteristic of Alzheimer's disease, cognitive impairment affects memory, attention, and other thinking abilities that significantly impact daily functioning," said Eiry W. Roberts, M.D., Chief Medical Officer, Neurocrine Biosciences . "The advancement of NBI-'567 reflects our commitment to delivering new treatment options for this vulnerable population, in addition to our broader strategy to explore the potential of selectively targeting muscarinic receptors across a range of neurological and psychiatric conditions." This Phase 2 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study will enroll approximately 135 adults ages 50 to 85 with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease who are receiving stable treatment with an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor. Participants will be randomized across a high or low dose level of NBI-'567 administered once daily. Over the 12-week treatment period, the study will assess the efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of NBI-'567 compared with placebo. The primary efficacy endpoint is change from baseline in a Neuropsychological Test Battery composite score at Week 12. Secondary endpoints include changes from baseline in ADAS-Cog13 and CDR Sum of Boxes at Week 12. Visit ClinicalTrials.gov for more information about the study (NBI-1117567-ADC2038).

VK2375 is being developed in both oral and subcutaneous formulations for the potential treatment of various metabolic disorders such as obesity. SUNRISE-2 will enroll adults with type 2 diabetes who are obese or overweight. Participants in both trials will be randomly assigned to one of four treatment groups receiving once-daily VK2735 doses of 27.5 mg, 35 mg, 55 mg, or placebo. lead: Roche presents new Phase III one-year data for vamikibart in uveitic macular edema (UME), a serious cause of vision loss 2026-10-10 In the MEERKAT and SANDCAT studies, vamikibart demonstrated sustained improvements in vision and reductions in macular thickness in patients with UME at 52 weeks 1,2 UME is the leading cause of moderate and severe vision loss in patients with uveitis, posing a significant risk of blindness if left untreated 3,4 The FDA has accepted Roche's Biologics License Application (BLA), with an approval decision expected by July 2027 Basel, 10 October 2026 - Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today new one-year data from the Phase III MEERKAT and SANDCAT studies evaluating investigational vamikibart compared with a sham procedure that mimics intravitreal (IVT) injections in adults with uveitic macular edema (UME). Across both studies, data continue to support the potential for rapid and sustained improvements in vision and reductions in macular thickness (swelling in the back of the eye due to retinal fluid) with vamikibart treatment. The data were presented at the American Academy of Ophthalmology 2026 Annual Meeting (AAO 2026) in New Orleans, LA. 1 Additionally, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted Roche’s Biologics License Application (BLA) for vamikibart for the treatment of UME. The filing acceptance is based on the results from the MEERKAT and SANDCAT studies. The FDA is expected to make a decision on approval by July 2027. If approved, vamikibart would be the first non-steroid targeted treatment for UME, with potential to establish a new standard of care. Regulatory submissions have also been filed and accepted in the European Union, China and Japan. “These one-year results strengthen vamikibart’s clinical profile, confirming that initial visual and anatomical improvements are maintained over 52 weeks,” said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. “The acceptance of our application by the FDA and other regulatory bodies around the world brings us closer to offering a transformative, non-steroid therapy for people living with this sight-threatening condition.” “Currently, UME is commonly treated with off-label therapies or ocular steroids, the latter carrying significant long-term side effects like glaucoma and cataract formation,” said Nisha Acharya, M.D., M.S., Distinguished Professor of Ophthalmology at UCSF and Director of the Uveitis and Ocular Inflammatory Disease Service. “Vamikibart is the first non-steroid targeted therapy to demonstrate meaningful and sustained visual and anatomical improvements in people with UME, offering a potential new treatment option that directly targets the inflammation driving this sight-threatening condition.” The 16-week primary analysis results were presented at the AAO meeting in October 2025. 2 In both MEERKAT and SANDCAT at 52 weeks, a numerically higher proportion of vamikibart-treated patients achieved vision gains compared to sham treatment on the primary endpoint. Key secondary endpoints showed this benefit was maintained, with sustained improvements in average change from baseline in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and average change from baseline in central subfield thickness (CST), a key measure of macular edema. Vamikibart demonstrated durable clinical benefit with a low treatment burden: approximately two-thirds of eligible patients required no retreatment after 16 weeks, while the majority of those who did required only one additional injection. Vamikibart was well tolerated, maintaining a favourable safety profile, with a low incidence of treatment-related ocular adverse events (AEs) and intraocular inflammation (IOI) events. 1 UME is the leading cause of moderate-to-severe vision loss in individuals with uveitis, predominantly affecting working-age adults. 3,4 Approximately 20% of UME patients progress to sustained blindness within three years of diagnosis. 5

The primary endpoint was change from baseline in the ratio of villus height-to-crypt depth (Vh:Cd) at day 78 versus placebo, aimed at determining whether FB102 protects the intestine from gluten-induced damage over the challenge period.

The decision is based on the recommendation from an Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) to stop the study for futility following an interim analysis. The IDMC concluded that the UNITY study is unable to meet its primary endpoint. Safety was consistent with efgartigimod's established profile and no new safety signals were identified. To be eligible, patients had to meet the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for primary Sjögren's disease, test positive for anti-Ro/SSA autoantibodies and have moderate-to-severe systemic disease activity (clinESSDAI ≥6) while receiving stable background standard of care. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive weekly efgartigimod SC or placebo during the double-blind treatment period. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in systemic disease activity, as measured by the clinical EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (clinESSDAI), at Week 48. Key secondary endpoints included the proportion of patients achieving low disease activity (clinESSDAI <5), responder status on the Sjögren's Tool for Assessing Response (STAR), change in patient-reported symptoms as measured by the Diary of Sjögren's Symptoms Assessment (DiSSA), and safety and tolerability.

lead: Rocket Pharmaceuticals Highlights FDA-Aligned Pivotal Phase 2 Trial and Updated Clinical Findings for RP-A501 Following Danon Disease Investor Webinar Oct 7, 2026 | PDF Version CRANBURY, N.J. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 7, 2026-- Rocket Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: RCKT), a fully integrated commercial-stage biotechnology company advancing genetic medicines for rare and life-threatening diseases, highlighted key findings and development milestones presented during its October 6 Danon disease investor webinar. The update outlined a defined path to completing the FDA -aligned pivotal Phase 2 trial, highlighted sustained biological activity in longer-term Phase 1 follow-up and reported encouraging initial safety observations in the first three patients treated under the modified protocol. Key highlights included: Pivotal Phase 2 trial: The FDA -aligned pivotal efficacy population includes 12 male patients receiving commercial-grade RP-A501 at the recalibrated dose. The first three patients treated under the modified protocol count toward this population. Trial success requires at least seven patients to meet both response criteria at 12 months: myocardial LAMP2 protein expression of at least Grade 1 and a reduction in left ventricular mass index of at least 10% from baseline. These co-primary endpoints are intended to support a potential accelerated approval pathway. Modified protocol: The first three patients treated at the recalibrated dose completed the protocol-specified initial observation period without clinical or laboratory evidence of thrombotic microangiopathy or capillary leak syndrome, as reported during the webinar. Follow-up is ongoing, and these initial observations are preliminary. Phase 1 results: At approximately 12 months, all six patients in the principal Phase 1 analysis demonstrated myocardial LAMP2 protein expression and at least a 10% reduction in left ventricular mass index. At follow-up of approximately three to seven years, left ventricular mass index was below baseline in five of six patients, with reductions of at least 10% in four patients. All six patients also had sustained reduction of cardiac biomarkers and improvements of quality of life. Original-dose Phase 2 results: Three of four patients with longitudinal efficacy assessments achieved at least a 10% reduction in left ventricular mass index. Safety findings from the original-dose study, including thrombotic microangiopathy and a fatal serious adverse reaction, informed the recalibrated dose, revised immunomodulation regimen and enhanced safety monitoring now in place. Patient population: Genetic and clinical analyses converged on a modeled U.S . Danon disease population of approximately 10,000–11,000, including 4,000 males. Rocket’s initial focus is males with symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Upcoming milestones: Rocket expects to complete pivotal trial dosing by mid-2027, with topline results anticipated mid-2028. A replay of the webinar and the accompanying presentation are available in the Investors section of Rocket’s website at ir.rocketpharma.com .

lead: Revolution Medicines Begins Treating Patients in Phase 3 RASolute 309 Trial Evaluating RASONQUE™ (daraxonrasib) Plus Zoldonrasib as First-Line Treatment for Metastatic RAS G12D Pancreatic Cancer October 5, 2026 PDF Version REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Revolution Medicines, Inc. (Nasdaq: RVMD), a global, commercial-stage oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced that it has begun treating patients in RASolute 309, a global, randomized Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the combination of RASONQUE (daraxonrasib), a RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor, and zoldonrasib, an investigational RAS(ON) G12D-selective inhibitor, as a first-line treatment in adult patients with metastatic RAS G12D pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC). “RAS G12D is the most common RAS variant in PDAC,” said Alan Sandler, M.D., chief development officer of Revolution Medicines. “In preclinical studies, the combination of RAS(ON) multi-selective and G12D-selective inhibitors achieved deeper and more sustained suppression of RAS signaling than either agent alone, accompanied by greater tumor control. Likewise, initial clinical data showed that RASONQUE plus zoldonrasib delivered compelling antitumor activity in patients with previously treated metastatic PDAC, with a manageable safety and tolerability profile. In the context of the unmet need in this patient population, these findings informed the design of the first-line RASolute 309 trial in patients with PDAC. RASolute 309 is the first Phase 3 study evaluating a RAS(ON) inhibitor doublet approach and it marks an important milestone in our efforts to advance a range of potential treatment options for patients with RAS-driven cancers across tumor types and treatment settings.” RASolute 309 ( NCT07805954 ) is a global, randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial evaluating RASONQUE plus zoldonrasib compared with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) as a first-line treatment in adult patients with metastatic RAS G12D PDAC. The dual primary endpoints are progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival. Key secondary endpoints include PFS, objective response rate, duration of response, safety and tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and patient-reported outcomes.

LNTH-2401 is an investigational gallium-68-labeled positron emission tomography (PET) imaging agent that targets the gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR), a biomarker that is highly expressed in many prostate cancers. SPARROW is an open-label, non-randomized, multicenter Phase 2/3 study that includes an initial Phase 2 dose optimization period followed by a Phase 3 diagnostic performance period. The Phase 3 co-primary endpoints are sensitivity and specificity of LNTH-2401 PET/CT imaging compared with histopathology. The Phase 3 portion of the trial is expected to enroll approximately 400 participants and will evaluate diagnostic performance, safety and tolerability. “Accurate characterization of disease remains critically important in prostate cancer, particularly as treatment decisions become increasingly personalized,” said Harshad R. Kulkarni , MD, Chief Medical Advisor at BAMF Health and a principal investigator in the SPARROW study. “We are pleased to have dosed the first patient at BAMF Health , where our integrated molecular imaging, radiopharmacy and clinical trials infrastructure supports the evaluation of emerging radiopharmaceutical technologies. Emerging research suggests GRPR-targeted imaging may provide additional insight in certain tumors that are not optimally characterized using PSMA-directed approaches alone. 1 “Dosing the first patient in SPARROW represents a significant step forward for our pipeline and underscores our commitment to advancing innovative radiopharmaceuticals across the prostate cancer care continuum,” said Ludger Dinkelborg, Head of Research and Development at Lantheus . “As the leader in prostate cancer PSMA PET imaging, LNTH-2401 has the potential to expand our understanding of prostate cancer biology through a complementary imaging target. Arlo-cel is a potential first-in-class autologous G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D)-directed CAR T cell therapy. As a CAR T cell therapy designed to be administered as a single infusion,* arlo-cel potentially represents a differentiated approach for patients with heavily pretreated relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. Results show the study met its primary endpoint with arlo-cel demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful overall response rate (ORR) in patients with quadruple-class exposed RRMM who had received four or more prior lines of therapy. Hoch , president, Cell Therapy Organization, Bristol Myers Squibb. “These topline results support arlo-cel's potential benefit for patients while showing a safety profile consistent with expectations. They underscore our continued innovation in multiple myeloma and highlight the value of targeting alternative proteins, like GPRC5D, with the power of cell therapy to transform outcomes, laying the foundation for arlo-cel to become an important treatment option for this emerging group of patients who have been exposed to prior BCMA-targeted therapies.” Bristol Myers Squibb thanks the patients and investigators who are participating in the QUINTESSENTIAL clinical trial. lead: Vor Completes Enrollment of Global Phase 3 UPSTREAM MG Trial and Expands Telitacicept Global Franchise into Ocular Myasthenia Gravis September 8, 2026 PDF Version Topline results from UPSTREAM MG’s 24-week primary endpoint remain on track for first half of 2027 Global Phase 3 ocular myasthenia gravis (oMG) registrational trial, UPSTREAM oMG, broadens telitacicept development across the myasthenia gravis (MG) spectrum; first patient dosing anticipated in the first half of 2027 BOSTON, Sept. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vor Bio (Nasdaq: VOR), a clinical-stage biotechnology company transforming the treatment of autoimmune diseases, today announced the completion of enrollment in UPSTREAM MG, its global Phase 3 registrational trial evaluating telitacicept for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG). Topline results from the 24-week primary endpoint remain expected in the first half of 2027. Vor Bio also plans to initiate UPSTREAM oMG, a global Phase 3 registrational trial evaluating telitacicept for the treatment of patients with ocular myasthenia gravis, with the first patient dosing anticipated in the first half of 2027. The program is being advanced as a registrational expansion of Vor Bio’s existing MG development program, supporting potential future label expansion across the myasthenia gravis spectrum and builds on the broader clinical experience with telitacicept in MG, including RemeGen’s ongoing Phase 3 trial in oMG in China. “Completing enrollment in UPSTREAM MG brings us closer to a defining Phase 3 readout in the first half of 2027,” said Jean-Paul Kress, M.D., Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Vor Bio. “We are deeply grateful to the patients whose participation and commitment made this milestone possible, as well as to our investigators, key opinion leaders, partners, and the Vor team for their exceptional execution. Additionally, our decision to expand into ocular MG reflects our growing conviction that telitacicept has the potential to be a foundational therapy across MG. More broadly, we see expansion in MG as the first step of a much larger campaign for telitacicept. With multiple global programs advancing, we are executing on our near-term priorities while building a broad, enduring autoimmune franchise.” “Telitacicept represents a promising and differentiated approach to the treatment of myasthenia gravis through targeted B-cell modulation,” said James F. Howard, Jr., M.D., UNC School of Medicine. “By inhibiting both BAFF and APRIL, telitacicept has the potential to address key drivers of disease biology through a broader mechanism than current downstream therapies focused primarily on circulating IgG reduction and without complete B-cell depletion. The clinical data generated to date provide a strong rationale for continued development. I look forward to the results of this global study and the potential impact they may have for our patients living with myasthenia gravis. The expansion of the development program into ocular myasthenia gravis is also an important step forward. Ocular symptoms can significantly affect daily functioning and quality of life, and there remains a need for treatment options that may reduce reliance on long-term corticosteroid use while helping to effectively manage disease symptoms.” “Individuals living with myasthenia gravis need more treatment options that can provide meaningful and sustained control of a disease that can profoundly affect everyday life. "We look forward to the results and are encouraged by the expansion into ocular MG, which extends the effort to bring new treatment options to patients across the MG spectrum.”

lead: PepGen to Advance PGN-EDODM1 Into Highest Dose Cohort in Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 Study Following DSMB Review August 6, 2026 PDF Version – DSMB also recommended dose escalation in FREEDOM-OLE from 5 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg – BOSTON --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- PepGen Inc. (Nasdaq: PEPG), a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing the next generation of oligonucleotide therapies with the goal of transforming the treatment of severe neuromuscular and neurological diseases, today announced that an independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) has recommended advancing the ongoing Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 study evaluating PGN-EDODM1 in participants with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) into the third and highest multiple ascending dose (MAD) cohort of 12.5 mg/kg, with no recommended changes to the study protocol. The DSMB also recommended dose escalation in the open-label extension (OLE) study from 5 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg. Notably, 6 of 8 participants from the 5 mg/kg FREEDOM2 cohort have elected to enroll in the OLE, bringing total OLE enrollment to 16 participants. The recommendation followed a review of available safety data from the fully enrolled 10 mg/kg MAD cohort and the OLE study. PGN-EDODM1 remains generally well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities reported in FREEDOM2 or the OLE to date. Repeat dosing at both the 5 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg dose levels shows no evidence of cumulative toxicity, and no treatment discontinuations were reported in FREEDOM2 or the OLE. “The DSMB's recommendation to advance FREEDOM2 into the highest planned dose level in the study and escalate dosing in the OLE supports the encouraging safety profile of PGN-EDODM1 following multiple months of treatment,” said James McArthur , PhD, President and Chief Executive Officer of PepGen . “In the FREEDOM2 study, 7 of 8 participants in the 10 mg/kg cohort have now completed dosing. We look forward to reporting additional safety, splicing and functional data from FREEDOM2 as we continue to evaluate the potential of PGN-EDODM1 to address the root cause of disease across multiple organ systems.” The Company expects to report results from the fully enrolled 10 mg/kg FREEDOM2 cohort in November. Results from the 12.5 mg/kg cohort are expected in the first half of 2027, at which time PepGen plans to engage with regulators in an end of Phase 2 meeting to discuss plans for the registrational program.
